claim:
Let \(T=EC_{\{f\}}\) be the complete model completion of the empty theory in the language of one unary function. For \(p\in S_n(T)\), form the quotient of the term forest \(\{f^m(x_i):1\le i\le n,\ m<\omega\}\) by the equalities in \(p\), and let \(\rho(p)\) be the number of infinite connected components of this quotient functional graph. Then for every \(n\ge1\) and every \(0\le k\le n\),
\[
S_n(T)^{(k)}=\{p\in S_n(T):\rho(p)\ge k\},
\]
where \(S_n(T)^{(k)}\) denotes the \(k\)-th Cantor--Bendixson derivative. Hence the Cantor--Bendixson rank of \(p\) is exactly \(\rho(p)\), \(S_n(T)^{(n)}\) is the singleton type asserting that all terms \(f^a(x_i)\) are pairwise distinct, and \(S_n(T)^{(n+1)}=\varnothing\). Since \(S_n(T)\) is countable compact metrizable, it follows that
\[
S_n(T)\cong \omega^n+1
\]
for every \(n\ge1\).
integrity: The primary ingredients are quantifier elimination/model completion and countability/omega-stability from modern eligible sources. The retained contribution is the exact Cantor--Bendixson derivative formula in terms of infinite forward components and its ordinal-space corollary. Same-model review explicitly separates prior cardinality/stability results from the new topological computation.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats only complete finite-tuple types over the empty set in the language with exactly one unary function.

The homeomorphism uses the standard finite-height classification of countable compact metrizable scattered spaces; the package includes the needed finite-rank induction rather than claiming that topological classification as new.
Equivalent rank calculations may exist in older unary-function or stability-theory literature under different terminology; targeted searches found none.
title: Generic unary functions have ordinal type spaces \(\omega^n+1\)
